q: Which scrotal swelling feels like a bag of worms and fills when the man stands?
x: Dilated pampiniform veins fill with blood when the man stands and empty when he lies down, so they feel like a bag of worms. Blood absorbs light, so a varicocele does not transilluminate.

w.Hydrocele: A hydrocele is a smooth collection of clear fluid around the testis. It transilluminates and does not feel like a tangle of cords.
w.Hematocele: A hematocele is blood in the tunica vaginalis after trauma. It is a tense, dark swelling that follows an injury, not a soft tangle that changes with posture.
w.Spermatocele: A spermatocele is a smooth cyst above and behind the testis that transilluminates. It does not change with posture.
w.Germ cell tumor: A germ cell tumor is a firm, painless mass inside the testis that does not change with standing or lying, unlike a soft tangle of veins.

pt.say: The varicocele row sits in the cord and reads bag of worms, worse standing, which describes dilated pampiniform veins that fill when the man stands.

q: Which scrotal collection is blood within the tunica vaginalis after blunt trauma?
x: A hematocele is blood in the tunica vaginalis after trauma, so the swelling stays dark when a light is held behind it. A hard blow can also tear the tunica albuginea, a testicular rupture that needs prompt surgery.

w.Hydrocele: A hydrocele is also a collection in the tunica vaginalis, but it holds clear fluid, so it glows, and it develops slowly rather than after an injury.
w.Varicocele: A varicocele is dilated veins in the spermatic cord, a soft bag of worms above the testis. It is not a collection of blood in the tunica vaginalis.
w.Spermatocele: A spermatocele is a sperm-filled cyst of the epididymis above and behind the testis, and it transilluminates.
w.Inguinal hernia: An indirect inguinal hernia can descend into the scrotum, but it holds bowel or omentum and reduces when lying down. It is not blood from trauma.

pt.say: The hematocele row shows blood in the tunica vaginalis after trauma, which stays dark rather than glowing, unlike the fluid collections beside it.

q: Which scrotal cyst lies above and behind the testis, separate from it?
x: A spermatocele is a sperm-filled cyst of the epididymis that can be felt apart from the testis. It transilluminates and is benign. A mass that cannot be separated from the testis is a tumor until proven otherwise.

w.Hydrocele: A hydrocele surrounds the testis within the tunica vaginalis, so the testis cannot be felt separately from the fluid.
w.Hematocele: A hematocele is blood in the tunica vaginalis after trauma. It surrounds the testis and stays dark, and it is not a discrete cyst above the testis.
w.Varicocele: A varicocele is a soft tangle of dilated veins in the cord. It fills on standing and does not transilluminate.
w.Germ cell tumor: A germ cell tumor is a firm solid mass inside the testis that cannot be separated from it and stays dark with a light.

pt.say: The spermatocele row sits above and behind the testis as a sperm-filled epididymal cyst that is separate from it and glows with light.

q: What is the name of the pain relief seen when the testis is lifted, which favors epididymitis?
x: Prehn sign is the relief of pain when the testis is lifted. It favors epididymitis, because lifting eases the pull on the inflamed epididymis, while torsion gives no relief. It is unreliable and must never delay surgery when torsion is suspected.

w.Cremasteric reflex: The cremasteric reflex is lifting of the testis when the inner thigh is stroked. It is present in epididymitis and absent in torsion, but it is a reflex, not a response to lifting.
w.Blue dot sign: The blue dot sign is a bluish spot seen through the scrotal skin at the upper pole in a torsed appendix testis.
w.Whirlpool sign: The whirlpool sign is the spiral of twisted cord seen on ultrasound in testicular torsion. It is unrelated to pain relief.
w.Carnett sign: Carnett sign is increased abdominal wall pain when the muscles are tensed. It separates wall pain from visceral pain and is unrelated to the testis.

pt.say: In the lifting testis row, epididymitis shows relief, called the Prehn sign, while torsion shows no relief.

q: Which anatomic variant lets the testis hang free in the scrotum and twist on its cord?
x: In bell-clapper deformity the tunica vaginalis attaches too high on the cord, so the testis hangs free inside it like a clapper in a bell and can twist. The defect is usually bilateral, so surgery fixes both testes.

w.Patent processus vaginalis: A patent processus vaginalis leaves a channel to the peritoneal cavity, allowing a communicating hydrocele or an indirect inguinal hernia. It does not make a testis hang free and twist.
w.Retractile testis: A retractile testis is a normal variant in which the cremaster pulls the testis up toward the groin. It comes down easily and does not twist on its cord.
w.Spermatic cord lipoma: A lipoma of the cord is a soft fatty mass that mimics an inguinal hernia. It does not change how the testis is anchored.
w.Epididymal cyst: An epididymal cyst is a benign sperm-filled swelling above and behind the testis. It does not alter how the testis is anchored.

pt.say: The bell-clapper panel shows a testis hanging free in a horizontal lie with a twisted spermatic cord, the deformity that allows torsion.

q: Which nerve forms the motor limb of the cremasteric reflex?
o: Genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve
Femoral branch of the genitofemoral nerve
x: Stroking the inner thigh sends signals up the femoral branch of the genitofemoral nerve. The genital branch carries the motor signal that makes the cremaster lift the testis. The reflex is absent in torsion.

w.Femoral branch of the genitofemoral nerv: The femoral branch is the sensory limb, carrying signals from the skin of the upper inner thigh. The genital branch carries the motor output to the cremaster.
w.Ilioinguinal nerve: The ilioinguinal nerve supplies the skin of the front of the scrotum and the root of the penis. It is not part of the cremasteric reflex arc.
w.Pudendal nerve: The pudendal nerve supplies the perineum, back of the scrotum and penile muscles and carries the bulbocavernosus reflex, not the cremasteric reflex.
w.Iliohypogastric nerve: The iliohypogastric nerve supplies skin above the pubis and muscles of the lower abdominal wall, not the cremaster muscle.

q: Which tumor marker is expressed by seminoma cells and by germ cell neoplasia in situ?
x: PLAP, placental alkaline phosphatase, is expressed by seminoma cells and by germ cell neoplasia in situ. AFP is never raised in pure seminoma, and hCG may be mildly raised from scattered syncytiotrophoblast cells.

w.AFP: AFP is made by yolk sac elements and signals a nonseminomatous component. A pure seminoma never raises it.
w.CA-125: CA-125 is an ovarian epithelial tumor marker, particularly for serous ovarian cancers. It has no role in testicular germ cell tumors.
w.PSA: PSA is a prostate-specific protease used to follow prostate cancer. Testicular germ cells do not make it.
w.CA 19-9: CA 19-9 is a marker for pancreatic and biliary cancers. Testicular germ cell tumors do not express it.

pt.say: The seminoma box lists PLAP positive and AFP never raised, so placental alkaline phosphatase is the marker that seminoma cells express.

q: Which chromosomal abnormality marks most testicular germ cell tumors?
x: Isochromosome 12p, two copies of the short arm of chromosome 12 on one chromosome, is found in most testicular germ cell tumors, seminomatous and nonseminomatous, which arise from germ cell neoplasia in situ.

w.t(9;22) Philadelphia chromosome: The t(9;22) Philadelphia chromosome creates the BCR-ABL fusion in chronic myeloid leukemia. It is not a feature of testicular germ cell tumors.
w.t(8;14) translocation: The t(8;14) translocation puts MYC under immunoglobulin heavy chain control in Burkitt lymphoma, not in germ cell tumors.
w.Deletion of 5q: Deletion of 5q is a feature of myelodysplastic syndrome and of the APC gene region in colon polyposis, not of testicular germ cell tumors.
w.Monosomy 7: Monosomy 7 is a marker of myelodysplasia and acute myeloid leukemia, often after chemotherapy. It is not a mark of testicular germ cell tumors.

pt.say: The germ cell tumor branch lists isochromosome 12p beside the age range and the GCNIS precursor, marking the shared cytogenetic change of germ cell tumors.

q: Which testicular germ cell tumor spreads early through the blood to the lungs?
x: Choriocarcinoma is made of syncytiotrophoblast and cytotrophoblast. It invades vessels and spreads through the blood to the lungs and brain, with very high hCG. Most other germ cell tumors spread first to para-aortic lymph nodes.

w.Seminoma: Seminoma spreads mainly through lymphatics to para-aortic nodes, late in its course, and has an excellent prognosis.
w.Embryonal carcinoma: Embryonal carcinoma is aggressive and can spread by blood, but lymphatic spread to retroperitoneal nodes comes first, and it lacks the extreme hCG of choriocarcinoma.
w.Yolk sac tumor: Yolk sac tumor in young boys usually presents localized with a high AFP. It is not defined by early blood-borne lung metastases.
w.Teratoma: Teratoma contains mixed tissues from three germ layers, and in adult men it can metastasize. It is not the classic early blood-borne tumor.

pt.say: The choriocarcinoma box reads trophoblast cells, hCG very high, and blood spread to lungs, so it is the tumor that spreads early through the blood.

q: Which testicular germ cell tumor is highly radiosensitive and has the best prognosis?
x: Seminoma's uniform fried-egg cells and lymphocyte-rich septa respond well to radiation and chemotherapy. It spreads late and through lymphatics, so early-stage disease is almost always cured.

w.Embryonal carcinoma: Embryonal carcinoma is aggressive and usually mixed with other elements, so its outlook is worse than seminoma.
w.Yolk sac tumor: Yolk sac tumor has a good prognosis in young boys, but in adults it appears within mixed tumors, which behave more aggressively than seminoma.
w.Choriocarcinoma: Choriocarcinoma has the worst prognosis of the germ cell tumors because it spreads early through the blood.
w.Teratoma: Teratoma contains tissues from all three germ layers, and mature-looking teratoma can still metastasize in adult men. It is not the tumor with the best prognosis.

pt.say: The seminoma box lists fried-egg cells, PLAP positive, radiosensitive and best prognosis, which distinguishes it from the nonseminomatous tumors.

q: Which germ cell tumor contains tissue from all three germ layers and can metastasize in adult men even when it looks mature?
x: Teratoma contains tissues from all three germ layers, such as cartilage, skin and neural tissue. In adult men even a mature-looking teratoma has malignant potential.

w.Seminoma: Seminoma is a uniform population of clear fried-egg cells. It shows no cartilage, skin or neural tissue from different germ layers.
w.Embryonal carcinoma: Embryonal carcinoma is a hemorrhagic tumor of primitive cells and shows no differentiated tissues.
w.Yolk sac tumor: Yolk sac tumor is recognized by Schiller-Duval bodies and a high AFP. It does not contain tissues from all three germ layers.
w.Choriocarcinoma: Choriocarcinoma consists of trophoblastic cells with very high hCG and hemorrhage. It does not contain tissues from all three germ layers.

pt.say: The teratoma box reads three germ layers and malignant in adult men, so teratoma is the tumor that can metastasize even when it looks mature.

q: Which testicular tumor causes precocious puberty in a boy while AFP and hCG stay normal?
x: A Leydig cell tumor is a sex cord-stromal tumor that makes androgens, causing precocious puberty in boys. Estrogens made from aromatization cause gynecomastia in men. AFP and hCG remain normal, and Reinke crystals are found on histology.

w.Seminoma: Seminoma occurs in adult men and makes no sex steroids, so it does not cause precocious puberty.
w.Yolk sac tumor: Yolk sac tumor affects boys under 3 and secretes AFP, but it does not secrete androgens.
w.Embryonal carcinoma: Embryonal carcinoma is a hemorrhagic germ cell tumor of young adults with variable AFP and hCG and no steroid secretion.
w.Lymphoma: Testicular lymphoma affects older men with bilateral painless enlargement, not boys with early virilization.

pt.say: The sex cord-stromal box lists Leydig tumors with Reinke crystals and androgen or estrogen excess, which explains precocious puberty in boys with normal markers.

q: Which fetal structure guides the descent of the testis into the scrotum?
x: The gubernaculum anchors the testis to the developing scrotum and guides its descent. The processus vaginalis pushes through the inguinal canal ahead of the testis, and failure of descent is cryptorchidism.

w.Processus vaginalis: The processus vaginalis is the peritoneal outpouching through the inguinal canal that the testis follows. Its lower end becomes the tunica vaginalis, and if it stays open it causes a hydrocele or hernia.
w.Mesonephric duct: The mesonephric (Wolffian) duct becomes the epididymis, ductus deferens and seminal vesicle. It does not guide testicular descent.
w.Urogenital sinus: The urogenital sinus forms the bladder and urethra and, in men, the prostate and bulbourethral glands. It does not anchor the testis.
w.Genital tubercle: The genital tubercle becomes the glans penis under the influence of DHT. It has no role in moving the testis.

pt.say: The homologs figure lists the gubernaculum anchoring the testis in the scrotum and becoming the ovarian and round ligaments in females, so it is the structure that guides descent.

q: Which testicular tumor is the most common mass in men older than 60 and is often bilateral?
x: Lymphoma, usually diffuse large B-cell type, is the most common testicular mass after age 60. It often involves both testes and causes painless enlargement with normal AFP and hCG, unlike the germ cell tumors of younger men.

w.Seminoma: Seminoma peaks in the 30s and 40s and is almost always unilateral, with a normal AFP and sometimes a mildly raised hCG.
w.Leydig cell tumor: Leydig cell tumors are small unilateral nodules in boys and men that cause precocious puberty or gynecomastia.
w.Embryonal carcinoma: Embryonal carcinoma occurs in men in their 20s and 30s as a hemorrhagic mass and often raises AFP or hCG.
w.Sertoli cell tumor: Sertoli cell tumors are uncommon, usually benign and hormonally silent. They are not the leading testicular mass of older men.

pt.say: The lymphoma box reads most common mass after 60 and often bilateral, which separates it from the germ cell tumors of younger men.
